slides.texte_overlay:
hobbies that will pull you out
of your dopamine addiction

long walks without input

walk for 30 minutes with no music, no podcast and no phone. the first ten minutes feel boring, and then your brain finally starts thinking its own thoughts again.

puzzles with your hands

do a jigsaw puzzle, a crossword or a model kit in the evenings instead of scrolling. slow rewards teach your brain to enjoy effort again, not just the next hit.

one task timer

set a 25 minute timer and do one single task with your phone in another room. the itch to check something fades after a week, and your focus comes back stronger.

swapping the scroll

every time you reach for your feed, learn one real thing instead: a fact about space, a piece of history, the story of a painting. same 5 minutes, opposite effect on your brain.

gardening

grow one plant from seed and look after it every day. waiting weeks for something to grow is the perfect antidote to a brain trained to expect everything in seconds.
